subject: RFP bake-off: conditional matching credit, usage caps, and escrow mechanics
messages:
From: Clayton Wu <clayton@medsys.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-19T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: RFP bake-off — sandbox allowance question

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a follow-up about the credit structure for the bake-off window. They want clarity on two things: 1) whether credit matching is timeboxed to the first 30 days after kickoff, and 2) whether there are any usage caps per model family (we'll be testing both Llama-like and Mistral variants).

Can you send the proposed terms so our legal and procurement can review? Also attaching the RFP doc for context — you'll see the evaluation metrics and expected concurrency.

Best,
Clayton
Senior AI Engineer
MedSys AI

Attachment: MedSys_RFP_SLA.pdf (application/pdf)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Clayton Wu <clayton@medsys.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off — sandbox allowance question

Hi Clayton —

Appreciate the clear asks. We've sketched a proposal that aligns with your RFP while protecting platform economics. High-level:

- Conditional matching: Redwood will match up to $40k of MedSys consumption during the first 30 calendar days of the sanctioned bake-off (match is pro-rata and paid as credits).
- Escrow hold: To ensure fairness we request a nominal escrow of $5k from MedSys that will be refunded pro-rata if the matched usage is not exhausted. Escrow prevents duplicate stacking with other vendors.
- Model-family caps: Per-model family cap of 300k tokens for highest-capacity variants (e.g., 8B+), and 750k tokens for smaller families. This prevents runaway spend on long-context experiments.
- Measurement & rollback: If regression or unsupported prompts cause sustained service issues, Redwood reserves the right to pause matching and work with your team to remediate.

I'll put the full term sheet in a spreadsheet and shared drive. Ben and Marissa — looping you for pricing sign-off and operational notes (billing flow / how the credits show on invoices).

Would MedSys be open to a 45-day acceptance period on usage reporting to account for their internal logging?

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Strategic Account Exec
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposed-credit-terms.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-20T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off — sandbox allowance question

Quick internal — agree with the structure but recommend tightening the escrow refund triggers and clarifying audit windows. Suggested edits:

- Escrow refund: Full refund if total MedSys consumption < 20% of matched credits after 30 days; otherwise refund pro-rata.
- Auditing: Use both Redwood billing logs + MedSys export; disputes escalate to joint audit within the 45-day acceptance period.
- Promo constraint: Credits only apply to inference calls routed through the sanctioned project id; no credits for self-hosted / non-pinned variants.

Also propose a short SLA credit clause: if Redwood latency exceeds agreed SLO for more than 12 hours cumulative during the 30-day window, we reduce matched credit by 10% as the remediation (instead of refunds). Keeps remediation aligned.

If that sounds good I'll update the spreadsheet and draft a short addendum for procurement.

-Ben
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Clayton Wu <clayton@medsys.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Procure Team <procure@medsys.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off — sandbox allowance question

Olga, Ben —

Appreciate the fast turn. Procurement flagged two items: 1) they want the escrow amount to be applied toward the matched credits (not refunded separately) and 2) they'd like an explicit cadence for rollup reporting (we propose weekly consumption snapshots plus a final 45-day report).

On model caps: we may need an override for a single heavy test run (up to 1.2M tokens on an 8B+ instance) — this would be a one-time exception provided we give 48hr notice. Would Redwood accommodate that as part of the escrow mechanics?

If we can get language that the escrow is a credit-on-delivery (i.e., counts toward the match), Procurement can move faster.

Clayton
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Clayton Wu <clayton@medsys.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-23T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP bake-off — sandbox allowance question

Clayton —

Thanks — that's reasonable. Finalized positions below (we'll include them in the addendum sent to procurement):

1) Escrow-as-credit: MedSys escrow will be applied against matched credits. If escrow > actual matched consumption, Redwood refunds the delta within 30 days of final reconciliation.
2) One-time heavy run: We'll allow a single capped exception up to 1.2M tokens for an 8B+ test with 48hr notice; that run consumes from the model-family cap and the escrow/match pool.
3) Reporting cadence: Weekly consumption snapshots (CSV export) during the 30-day window plus final reconciliation at 45 days. Disputes go to joint audit.
4) SLA remediation: If latency or platform issues materially impact the bake-off, we commit to a remediation credit or pro-rated extension of the window; specifics will be in addendum.

Ben/Marissa/Karthik — please confirm sign-off on pricing floor and that this fits the promo governance so I can send to their procurement.

Olga
Senior Strategic Account Exec
Redwood Inference
